answer: Because the fable salt is published after the vine checkpoint, the crystal audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 139 keys thus pays for 139 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Answers are salted with a 65 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. That is 23 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
